paper_metadata.title: Ultrastrong 42CrMo/CoCrNi multilayer composites at cryogenic temperatures

evidence.quote: Here we fabricate a multilayer composite comprising 42CrMo steel and CoCrNi medium-entropy alloy via hot-rolling.

Among these, CoCrNi alloy stands out for its outstanding low-temperature strain-
hardening capability and ductility
Here we fabricate a multilayer composite comprising 42CrMo steel and CoCrNi medium-entropy alloy via hot-rolling.

Two 42CrMo/CoCrNi multilayer composites with layer thickness ratios of 4:1 and 2:1 were fabricated by hot-rolling stacks of 42CrMo steel and CoCrNi MEA with thickness of 2 mm and 0.5 mm, respectively. These composites are designated as L4/1 and L2/1, respectively.

Two 42CrMo/CoCrNi multilayer composites with layer thickness ratios of 4:1 and 2:1 were fabricated by hot-rolling stacks of 42CrMo steel and CoCrNi MEA with thickness of 2 mm and 0.5 mm, respectively. These composites are designated as L4/1 and L2/1, respectively.
Tensile tests of 42CrMo/CoCrNi composites were conducted at 298 K and 93 K, alongside stress – strain curves of 42CrMo steel for comparison ( Fig. 3 a).
The L4/1 and L2/1 samples were fabricated via hot-rolling at 1150 ℃ using a 40-layer alternating 42CrMo/CoCrNi stacks with ~ 90 % total thickness reduction.

HRTEM image ( Fig. 4 d) reveals characteristic deformation twins along with localized martensitic transformation from face-centered cubic (fcc) to hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structures.

The 42CrMo layer primarily deforms through dislocation activities ( Fig. 4 a), while the CoCrNi MEA accommodates deformation through high-density stacking faults (SFs) and extensive deformation twinning ( Fig. 4 b – d).
This unique morphology likely results from dynamic recrystallization during hot-rolling.
Cracks initiating in the 42CrMo layer are arrested by the ductile CoCrNi layer, contributing to the improved ductility of the composite at 93 K.
These mechanisms in the CoCrNi layer enhance strain-hardening and reduce localized stress concentrations, delaying crack propagation in the 42CrMo layer and preventing premature failure.
